key_insight: ODT predicts that heat transfer in turbulent concentric annular pipe flow is strongly affected by radius ratio, with near-wall temperature following a logarithmic rather than linear law, especially near the inner curved wall.
engineering_relevance: Radius-ratio-dependent Nusselt correlations and wall-scaling laws can improve thermal design of annular ducts, coaxial pipes, and similar curved-wall cooling/heating systems.
method: Stochastic one-dimensional turbulence (ODT) resolves viscous, conductive, and turbulent advective transport along a representative radial coordinate.
Parametric study spans radius ratio, curvature, Reynolds number, and two Prandtl numbers (0.71 and 0.025).
Boundary-layer analysis is used to derive wall-temperature laws and heat-transfer scaling relations.
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated against analytical boundary-layer expressions and numerical predictions across an extended parametric range, showing consistent radius-ratio effects and the need for log-law-based wall fits.
watch_item: A conventional linear near-wall temperature profile can be misleading in curved annular flows, so calibration and scaling should account for curvature and finite-Re effects.
paper_title: Numerical Simulation of Turbulent Concentric Annular Pipe Flow using One-Dimensional Turbulence (ODT): Part 2: Heat Transfer
